text:
Manny Malhotra's first season behind the Canucks bench has mostly been about losing. Vancouver is 5-17-1 with 11 points after 23 games, and before Sunday's 6-3 win over Vegas it had dropped seven straight. Then Nikita Tolopilo, in his first start of the season, stole Monday's 3-2 win in Utah. Two in a row feels like a pulse. It is not a turnaround yet.

The underlying numbers are the hard part. The Canucks get 39.79% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and allow 3.89 expected goals per 60 minutes. Our projection has them around 61 points, with essentially no path to the playoffs. If anything, the results have run a little ahead of the chances: they've scored 6.6 more goals than expected.

Goaltending has made it worse. Kevin Lankinen has an .802 save percentage over his last five starts, all losses, and 9.3 goals worse than expected. That is why Tolopilo's night matters beyond one win.

There are things worth watching. Brock Boeser has been the hot hand ("Boesvember," per Pass it to Bulis' Daniel Wagner), Liam Ohgren has five points in ten games, and Elias Pettersson is drawing Selke talk in the headlines. The young defence is learning in public: Zeev Buium and Filip Hronek have been on for 32% of the expected goals together. For a team this far out of the race, how those young players handle it is the season's real story.
headline: Two wins, and a long way still to climb
